Now I have everything needed to give a complete answer. ## `BrokerLifecycleManager` state machine Source: `server/src/main/java/org/apache/kafka/server/BrokerLifecycleManager.java` It's an event-driven state machine: all events run on a single-threaded `EventQueue`, and `state` (a `BrokerState`) is only ever written from that thread. It **starts in `BrokerState.NOT_RUNNING`** (field default at line 131). The intended path is: ``` NOT_RUNNING → STARTING → RECOVERY → RUNNING → PENDING_CONTROLLED_SHUTDOWN → SHUTTING_DOWN ``` ### Every `EventQueue.Event` class it handles | Event class | Sets `BrokerState`? | Enqueued by | |---|---|---| | **`StartupEvent`** | → `STARTING` (unconditionally) | `start()` (public API called by `KafkaBroker`/`BrokerServer` on boot) via `eventQueue.append(new StartupEvent(...))` | | **`RegistrationTimeoutEvent`** | none directly — if registration still hasn't succeeded, calls `eventQueue.beginShutdown("registrationTimeout")`, which drives the queue's built-in shutdown event | Scheduled deferred by `StartupEvent.run()` (`scheduleDeferred("initialRegistrationTimeout", ...)`) | | **`BrokerRegistrationResponseEvent`** | none directly (leaves state as-is; sets `registered = true` / `brokerEpoch` on success) | `BrokerRegistrationResponseHandler.onComplete`/`onTimeout` (the RPC completion callback), via `eventQueue.prepend(...)` | | **`CommunicationEvent`** | none — just decides whether to `sendBrokerHeartbeat()` or `sendBrokerRegistration()` | Scheduled deferred repeatedly via `scheduleNextCommunication(...)` (called after every registration/heartbeat response, success or failure) | | **`BrokerHeartbeatResponseEvent`** | → `RECOVERY` (from `STARTING`, once caught up)
→ `RUNNING` (from `RECOVERY`, once unfenced)
no state change while already `RUNNING`, `PENDING_CONTROLLED_SHUTDOWN` (may call `beginShutdown()` if controller says to exit), or `SHUTTING_DOWN` | `BrokerHeartbeatResponseHandler.onComplete`/`onTimeout` (RPC completion callback), via `eventQueue.prepend(...)` | | **`BeginControlledShutdownEvent`** | → `PENDING_CONTROLLED_SHUTDOWN` (only if currently `RUNNING`); if in any other state (except already `PENDING_CONTROLLED_SHUTDOWN`), it instead calls `beginShutdown()` | `beginControlledShutdown()` (public API), via `eventQueue.append(...)` | | **`ShutdownEvent`** | → `SHUTTING_DOWN` (always) | Passed as the queue's designated shutdown event when the `EventQueue` is constructed — fired when `eventQueue.beginShutdown(...)` is called (from `beginShutdown()`/`close()`, `RegistrationTimeoutEvent`, or internally by `BrokerHeartbeatResponseEvent` when the controller asks to exit) | | **`ResendBrokerRegistrationEvent`** | none — resets `registered = false` to force re-registration | Not shown being enqueued in this file (available as an internal trigger method, e.g. for feature/listener updates forcing re-registration) | | **`SetReadyToUnfenceEvent`** | none — sets `readyToUnfence = true` | Public method (e.g. called once broker startup/log-recovery work is complete) via `eventQueue.append(new SetReadyToUnfenceEvent())` | | **`OfflineDirEvent`** | none — records a log dir as offline in `offlineDirs` | Public `handleOfflineDir` API via `eventQueue.append(new OfflineDirEvent(directory))`, which also schedules an `OfflineDirBrokerFailureEvent` | | **`OfflineDirBrokerFailureEvent`** | none — if the offline dir was never acknowledged by the controller, calls `shutdownHook.run()` directly (bypassing the state machine) | Deferred by the offline-dir handling, via `eventQueue.scheduleDeferred("offlineDirFailure", ...)` | | **`CordonedDirEvent`** | none — updates `cordonedLogDirs` | Public API for cordoning log dirs, via `eventQueue.append(new CordonedDirEvent(directories))` | ### Notes - All state writes happen in exactly four places: `StartupEvent` (→STARTING), `BrokerHeartbeatResponseEvent` (→RECOVERY, →RUNNING), `BeginControlledShutdownEvent` (→PENDING_CONTROLLED_SHUTDOWN), and `ShutdownEvent` (→SHUTTING_DOWN). - `BrokerRegistrationResponseEvent` and `CommunicationEvent` never touch `state` — they only manage the `registered`/`communicationInFlight` bookkeeping and RPC retries. - `BrokerState` itself (in `metadata/src/main/java/org/apache/kafka/metadata/BrokerState.java`) documents the same linear transition diagram, plus an `UNKNOWN` catch-all state.
